title: “Slew of their foes seventy and five thousand” — the Greek has fifteen thousand

title: The scribes called “in the third month, that is, the month Sivan” — the Greek has the first month, Nisan
summary: The KJV, with the Hebrew, dates the letters written for the Jews to the twenty-third day of the third month, Sivan. Brenton’s Greek dates them to the twenty-third day of the first month, Nisan. Haman’s letters are dated in all three texts to the thirteenth day of the first month.

title: The day set to destroy the Jews: “the thirteenth day of the twelfth month” — the Greek has the lot fall on the fourteenth
summary: In the KJV, with the Hebrew, Haman’s letters set the thirteenth day of Adar. In Brenton’s Greek the lot falls on the fourteenth of Adar, the verse matching KJV 3:13 gives no day number, and the copy of the letter printed after it (a passage the KJV does not have) names the fourteenth. Later the Greek, like the KJV, has the thirteenth.
text: KJV Esther 3:7: “they cast Pur, that is, the lot, before Haman from day to day, and from month to month, to the twelfth month, that is, the month Adar” KJV Esther 3:13: “in one day, even upon the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, which is the month Adar” Hebrew (WLC) 3:7: מִיֹּ֧ום ׀ לְיֹ֛ום וּמֵחֹ֛דֶשׁ לְחֹ֥דֶשׁ שְׁנֵים־עָשָׂ֖ר הוּא־חֹ֥דֶשׁ אֲדָֽר [from day to day and from month to month, the twelfth, that is the month Adar]; 3:13: בְּיֹ֣ום אֶחָ֔ד בִּשְׁלֹושָׁ֥ה עָשָׂ֛ר לְחֹ֥דֶשׁ שְׁנֵים־עָשָׂ֖ר הוּא־חֹ֣דֶשׁ אֲדָ֑ר [in one day, on the thirteenth of the twelfth month, that is the month Adar]. [so as to destroy in one day the race of Mardochaeus; and the lot fell on the fourteenth of the month which is Adar]; 3:13: ἀφανίσαι τὸ γένος τῶν Ἰουδαίων ἐν ἡμέρᾳ μιᾷ μηνὸς δωδεκάτου, ὅς ἐστιν Ἀδὰρ [to destroy the race of the Jews in one day of the twelfth month, which is Adar]; the verse labelled 3:13f, in the copy of the letter: τῇ τεσσαρεσκαιδεκάτῃ τοῦ δωδεκάτου μηνὸς Ἄδαρ [on the fourteenth of the twelfth month Adar]. KJV Esther 8:12: “upon the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, which is the month Adar” Greek 8:12: τῇ τρισκαιδεκάτῃ τοῦ δωδεκάτου μηνὸς, ὅς ἐστιν Ἀδάρ [on the thirteenth of the twelfth month, which is Adar]. KJV 9:1: “in the twelfth month, that is, the month Adar, on the thirteenth day of the same” Greek 9:1: Ἐν γὰρ τῷ δωδεκάτῳ μηνὶ τρισκαιδεκάτῃ τοῦ μηνός, ὅς ἐστιν Ἀδάρ [for in the twelfth month, on the thirteenth of the month, which is Adar]. title: Mordecai “took for his own daughter” — the Greek has “he brought her up for a wife for himself”
summary: The KJV, with the Hebrew, says Mordecai took the orphaned Esther as his daughter. Brenton’s Greek of the same verse says he brought her up to be a wife for himself.
text: KJV Esther 2:7: “whom Mordecai, when her father and mother were dead, took for his own daughter” Hebrew (WLC) 2:7: לְקָחָ֧הּ מָרְדֳּכַ֛י לֹ֖ו לְבַֽת [Mordecai took her to himself for a daughter]. Septuagint (Brenton Greek) 2:7: ἐν δὲ τῷ μεταλλάξαι αὐτῆς τοὺς γονεῖς, ἐπαίδευσεν αὐτὴν ἑαυτῷ εἰς γυναῖκα [and when her parents died, he brought her up for himself as a wife]. KJV Esther 2:15: “the daughter of Abihail the uncle of Mordecai, who had taken her for his daughter” Hebrew 2:15: אֲשֶׁר֩ לָקַֽח־לֹ֨ו לְבַ֜ת [who had taken her to himself for a daughter]. The Greek of 2:15 has no such clause: Ἐσθὴρ τῆς θυγατρὸς Ἀμιναδὰβ ἀδελφοῦ πατρὸς Μαρδοχαίου εἰσελθεῖν πρὸς τὸν βασιλέα [Esther the daughter of Aminadab, brother of the father of Mardochaeus, to go in to the king]. Fetched from https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/17/2/ and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/ESG02.htm.
reasoning: “Daughter” and “wife” are different relations. In the Hebrew and the KJV Mordecai is Esther’s adoptive father; in the Greek he rears his cousin intending her as his own wife, and she is then taken to the king.

title: “On that night could not the king sleep” — the Greek says “the Lord removed sleep from the king”, and names God in three more verses
summary: In four verses that the KJV and the Hebrew also have, Brenton’s Greek names God or the Lord where they do not: Mordecai charges Esther to fear God (2:20) and to call upon the Lord (4:8), the Lord takes away the king’s sleep (6:1), and Haman is told that a living God is with Mordecai (6:13). A whole-word search of the packaged KJV of Esther finds neither “God” nor “Lord” anywhere in the book.
text: KJV Esther 6:1: “On that night could not the king sleep” Hebrew (WLC): בַּלַּ֣יְלָה הַה֔וּא נָדְדָ֖ה שְׁנַ֣ת הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ [in that night the sleep of the king fled]. Septuagint (Brenton Greek): Ὁ δε Κύριος ἀπέστησε τὸν ὕπνον ἀπὸ τοὺ βασιλέως τὴν νύκτα ἐκείνην [but the Lord removed sleep from the king that night]. KJV Esther 2:20: “for Esther did the commandment of Mordecai, like as when she was brought up with him” Hebrew: וְאֶת־מַאֲמַ֤ר מָרְדֳּכַי֙ אֶסְתֵּ֣ר עֹשָׂ֔ה [and the command of Mordecai Esther did]. Greek: οὕτως γὰρ ἐνετείλατο αὐτῇ Μαρδοχαῖος, φοβεῖσθαι τὸν Θεὸν, καὶ ποιεῖν τὰ προστάγματα αὐτοῦ [for so Mardochaeus commanded her, to fear God and to do his commandments]. KJV Esther 4:8: “to make supplication unto him, and to make request before him for her people” Hebrew: וּלְבַקֵּ֥שׁ מִלְּפָנָ֖יו עַל־עַמָּֽהּ [and to make request before him for her people], the last words of the verse. Greek, continuing after the matching words: ἐπικάλεσαι τὸν Κύριον, καὶ λάλησον τῷ βασιλεῖ περὶ ἡμῶν, ῥύσαι ἡμᾶς ἐκ θανάτου. [call upon the Lord, and speak to the king about us, to deliver us from death]. KJV Esther 6:13: “thou shalt not prevail against him, but shalt surely fall before him” Hebrew: כִּֽי־נָפֹ֥ול תִּפֹּ֖ול לְפָנָֽיו [but falling thou shalt fall before him], the last words of the verse. Greek: καὶ οὐ μὴ δύνῃ αὐτὸν ἀμύνασθαι, ὅτι Θεὸς ζῶν μετʼ αὐτοῦ. [and thou shalt not be able to withstand him, because a living God is with him]. Fetched from https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/17/6/, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/17/2/, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/17/4/, https://ebible.org/grcbrent/ESG06.htm, https://ebible.org/grcbrent/ESG02.htm and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/ESG04.htm.
reasoning: In the Hebrew and the KJV of these verses no one names God: the king cannot sleep, and Haman’s fall is foretold without any mention of God. The Greek states in each place that God is acting or is to be obeyed or called upon. That is a statement the KJV does not make in these passages.
scope: G applies at the four verses listed. The search is a word search of the ten chapters of the packaged KJV for “God”, “gods” and “Lord” in any letter case; it found nothing. It is not a claim about what the book implies. The Greek also names God many times in its lettered passages, which are not counted here because the KJV has no matching verses. title: In Shushan “on the spoil laid they not their hand” — the Greek has “and they plundered”
summary: The KJV, with the Hebrew, says three times that the Jews did not take spoil. Brenton’s Greek agrees the second and third time, but at 9:10, of the first day in Shushan, it says without a negative that they plundered.
text: KJV Esther 9:10: “slew they; but on the spoil laid they not their hand” Hebrew (WLC) 9:10: וּבַ֨בִּזָּ֔ה לֹ֥א שָׁלְח֖וּ אֶת־יָדָֽם [and on the spoil they did not put forth their hand]. Septuagint (Brenton Greek), the end of 9:10 and the start of 9:11: τοῦ ἐχθροῦ τῶν Ἰουδαίων, καὶ διήρπασαν ἐν αὐτῇ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ· [the enemy of the Jews, and they plundered on that same day]. KJV Esther 9:15: “but on the prey they laid not their hand” Greek 9:15: καὶ οὐδὲν διήρπασαν [and they plundered nothing]. KJV Esther 9:16: “but they laid not their hands on the prey” Greek 9:16: καὶ οὐδὲν διήρπασαν. Fetched from https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/17/9/ and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/ESG09.htm.
reasoning: At 9:10 the Greek uses the same verb as at 9:15 and 9:16 but without “nothing”, so that it affirms what the Hebrew and the KJV deny. On the first day in Shushan the Jews take no spoil in the KJV and take spoil in the Greek.
scope: G applies at 9:10. At 9:15 and 9:16 the three texts agree. The Greek of 9:10 prints no object for the verb, so it does not say what was plundered or from whom. title: “In the days of Ahasuerus” — the Greek of Esther calls the king Artaxerxes
summary: The KJV, with the Hebrew, calls the king of the book of Esther Ahasuerus. Brenton’s Greek calls him Artaxerxes. In Ezra 4:6–7 the KJV prints both names, Ahasuerus and Artaxerxes, in consecutive verses.
text: KJV Esther 1:1: “Now it came to pass in the days of Ahasuerus, (this is Ahasuerus which reigned, from India even unto Ethiopia” Hebrew (WLC) 1:1: וַיְהִ֖י בִּימֵ֣י אֲחַשְׁוֵרֹ֑ושׁ ה֣וּא אֲחַשְׁוֵרֹ֗ושׁ [and it came to pass in the days of Ahasuerus, that is Ahasuerus]. Septuagint (Brenton Greek), the verse labelled 1:1s, which follows a passage the KJV does not have: Καὶ ἐγένετο μετὰ τοὺς λόγους τούτους ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις Ἀρταξέρξου· οὗτος ὁ Ἀρταξέρξης ἀπὸ τῆς Ἰνδικῆς ἑκατὸν εἰκοσιεπτὰ χωρῶν ἐκράτησεν [and it came to pass after these things in the days of Artaxerxes; this Artaxerxes held a hundred and twenty-seven regions from India]. KJV Esther 1:2: “when the king Ahasuerus sat on the throne of his kingdom” Greek 1:2: ὅτε ἐθρονίσθη βασιλεὺς Ἀρταξέρξης. KJV 3:1: “After these things did king Ahasuerus promote Haman” Greek 3:1: ἐδόξασεν ὁ βασιλεὺς Ἀρταξέρξης Ἀμὰν. KJV 10:3: “For Mordecai the Jew was next unto king Ahasuerus” Greek 10:3: Ὁ δὲ Μαρδοχαῖος διεδέχετο τὸν βασιλέα Ἀρταξέρξην. KJV Ezra 4:6: “And in the reign of Ahasuerus, in the beginning of his reign” KJV Ezra 4:7: “And in the days of Artaxerxes wrote Bishlam” Brenton’s Greek of those two verses has other forms: 4:6 ἐν βασιλείᾳ Ἀσσουήρου, 4:7 ἐν ἡμέραις Ἀρθασασθὰ. Fetched from https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/17/1/, https://ebible.org/grcbrent/ESG01.htm, https://ebible.org/grcbrent/ESG03.htm, https://ebible.org/grcbrent/ESG10.htm and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/EZR04.htm.
reasoning: Ahasuerus and Artaxerxes are both names the KJV prints, in consecutive verses of Ezra 4, and Brenton’s Greek of Ezra keeps them apart as well. A reader of the Greek Esther is told the story happened under a king Artaxerxes; a reader of the KJV, under Ahasuerus.
scope: G applies at 1:1; the same difference of name runs through the book and is shown here at three more verses, not at every verse. This record compares the names printed. It does not say which historical king either name refers to, and it does not say the two texts mean different men. This compares the wording of three texts.
